html:
SMTO-CTX-0033 — That reference is a task note, not a saved result

GUID: 6da3764a-e122-57b8-8c87-1321ef1363dc
Slug: wrong-result-reference-kind
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: stored-result-recovery

What happened

  • The task tried to open one of its own notes as if it were the saved output of a command. SMTO pointed it to the right way to open notes. Nothing was run or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task continue and check its activity for a read of the note or folder. SMTO gives the task the exact correct way to open that note, so it can fix this itself.
  2. If the task keeps making the same mistake, select Steer and tell it that this item is one of its task notes and should be opened as a note, not as a saved result. A short instruction often stops the task from repeating the wrong kind of read.

What success looks like

  • The task opens the note or folder and continues its work.

If it still fails

  • If the task stops here, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask the task to rerun earlier steps; the note is already saved.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • read_result received a reference that resolves to accessible Task Context notebook content (an entry, request document, revision or folder) rather than an execution receipt, so the resolver redirected to task_context.read or task_context.list.

What this means

  • Known notebook entries, request documents, revisions and folders use Task Context read/list semantics. The resolver directs the caller to the corresponding tool instead of interpreting notebook content as receipt data. JSON pointers for read_result remain relative to receipt data.

Why this can happen

  • Known notebook entries, request documents, revisions and folders use Task Context read/list semantics. The resolver directs the caller to the corresponding tool instead of interpreting notebook content as receipt data. JSON pointers for read_result remain relative to receipt data.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the returned tool and reference; do not reuse receipt-data pointers against notebook content.

How to fix it

  • Follow next_action: use task_context.read for an entry or document, or task_context.list for a folder, with the same reference. read_result pointers are relative to receipt data only; do not treat notebook content as an execution receipt or rerun an operation to fix the reference kind.
  • Follow next_action using task_context.read for content or task_context.list for a folder.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the supplied notebook read/list action instead of repeating read_result unchanged.

How to verify the fix

  • The indicated notebook reader returns the intended content or directory listing.

What not to do

  • Do not treat task notes as execution receipts or rerun an operation to correct the reference kind.

Technical notes

  • This correction dispatches no operation and changes no notebook content.
  • Notebook content does not itself prove that an operation ran or completed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
